retrieval: A lesson is retrieved when at least two of its triggers occur (case-insensitive) in the case's objective, situation or evidence; at most three, highest count first, ties by id.

lessons.text: A detector that checks for a file name accepts an empty scaffold as finished work. Parse the content the step requires; an empty file beside a finished claim is worse than no file.

For anything whose job is to report, 'it ran' and 'its output arrived' are different questions. A configured, executing but mute verifier can look healthier than a skipped one; a change in cost without a change in output is the finding.
A day was lost to an access theory while every build log named a one-field configuration error. Read the build or job log's first error before reasoning about credentials.

Every capability probe first checks something known to exist. In zsh an unquoted parameter is not word-split, so a loop of multi-word subcommands tests nothing. Absence reported by an unvalidated probe gets written down as fact.
A ceiling that counts stale entries silently stops a board. Verify each counted item is live and fix the source of the stale entries; raising the ceiling hides the defect.

A setting that keeps being reversed carries no recorded reason. Unattended release gates favour reliability; attended pull-request runs favour speed. Write the trade-off beside the value and protect it with a test.
Concurrent worktrees can half-empty a shared dependency cache. Point this build at an intact private copy instead of deleting a directory another session may be resolving into.
Timeouts in a quota reader are unknown allowance, not exhaustion and not permission. Do not launch on an old reading; separate start-up latency from the account request and fix the bound.

A reviewer's optional notes are a severity judgement, not permission to change code outside its coverage. Apply them before asking it to clear; afterwards the later commit needs the reviewer to see it.
A filtered test run that matches nothing exits 0 having executed nothing. Read the executed and passed counts from that run's own result bundle before calling it a pass.
A job that mints an account-wide resource on every run exhausts it; retries and more runners consume it faster. Find what each run creates and stop creating it.
For a staleness refusal, ask what writes the timestamp, not how old it is. If only the refused run can refresh it, no amount of waiting clears it; size the guard to the cadence or change the writer.
